Apply mode is intentionally reported as failed with a not-implemented message instead of corrupting storage; the canonicalizer/journal/atomic-publish/rollback state machine remains a tracked follow-up.

Implemented the Apply phase of the P1 rollout migration (phase 2): CanonicalizeRollout replays a legacy rollout into canonical paginated JSONL - session_meta header rewritten to history_mode=paginated (history_base/subagent_history_start_ordinal cleared), legacy events converted to turn boundaries (task_started/task_complete) and Rust-shaped ItemCompleted events wrapping canonical TurnItems (UserMessage/AgentMessage via CoreTurnItemJSONFromSessionItem), consecutive ordinals on every line, staged at .{name}.paginated.tmp, durable .pending journal under rollout-migrations/, atomic rename over the source, journal removal after publish, and staged cleanup on failure. MigrateRollouts --apply now migrates eligible files (previously fail-closed). End-to-end verified: dry-run -> eligible, apply -> migrated, dry-run -> already_paginated, migrated file replays 2 items with correct preview/turns; staged/journal cleaned.

Completed two more Apply-phase submodules of the P1 rollout migration: (1) compressed .jsonl.zst sources stay compressed after migration - the staged plain JSONL is compressed to .{name}.paginated.zst.tmp and renamed over the source (mirroring Rust compress_rollout_to_path + publish), with staged/decompressed cleanup verified; (2) legacy ThreadRolledBack markers are replayed through the existing rollbackSessionItems turn-dropping semantics so rolled-back turns are excluded from the canonical output while surviving turns stay intact (mirroring Rust RollbackPlan visibility). Both pinned by unit tests: compressed migrate keeps compression and replays content with paginated header; rollback marker drops the rolled-back turn's records.

The projection lives in the app layer to avoid a rollout<->state import cycle; the rollout package stays storage-only. End-to-end verified: migrate-rollouts --apply generates thread_history_1.sqlite with 1 completed turn, 2 items, next_rollout_byte_offset covering the file, and next_rollout_ordinal=5 (meta+started+2 items+complete); unit test pins the projection rows and checkpoint.

Completed the subagent rollout migration semantics: a migrated subagent rollout now carries subagent_history_start_ordinal = the canonical writer's final ordinal (the first ordinal after all copied parent history), mirroring Rust rewrite_subagent_history_boundary + RolloutMigrationKind detection (source prefix subagent / thread_source subAgent* unless memory_consolidation). Unit test pins the subagent boundary value (meta+started+2 items = 4) and the ordinary-rollout unset behavior.

Added the rollout-maintenance lock, mirroring Rust rollout/src/maintenance.rs: a process-scoped nonblocking exclusive lock at .tmp/rollout-maintenance.lock (via gofrs/flock, cross-platform) coordinates rollout compression and migration, which both publish by renaming over an existing rollout path. MigrateRollouts Apply acquires the lock and reports SkippedBusy (untouched source) when another maintenance job holds it; WaitAcquireRolloutMaintenanceLock blocks for tests/callers that prefer to wait. Unit tests pin first/second-acquire exclusion, release-then-reacquire, wait timeout, and the busy outcome leaving the source unmigrated.

Aligned upstream #38902 (Honor per-environment shell variable policies): Go previously parsed/merged/validated shell_environment_policy but never applied it in the app-server turn path (shell tool / user shell / unified exec), and Rust now applies the selected turn environment's policy. Implemented: (1) EnvironmentConfig carries ShellEnvironmentPolicy (protocol parity) with thread inference (Rust inferred_environment_config) and JSON roundtrip for thread metadata; (2) the shell executor resolves the thread-derived policy with the environment's resolved policy winning and sets ShellRequest.EnvPolicy; (3) local shell/unified-exec build the command env via execpolicy.CreateEnv (inherit none/core/all, default excludes, exclude/include_only, set, filters) while the remote exec-server receives the policy as ExecEnvPolicy (replacing the hardcoded inherit-all default); (4) the env-policy logic moved from codex_go/exec into the leaf codex_go/execpolicy package (mirrors the codex-execpolicy crate split) so the tool layer can use it without an import cycle. Registered as contract shell-environment-policy-per-environment with fn-name-pinned differential TestShellEnvPolicyDifferentialLikeRustExecCommandUsesInstalledPolicy (Rust exec_command_uses_installed_environment_shell_policy_with_explicit_overrides) plus executor/runner/appserver dynamic tests.

Closed the pre-ledger P0 gap Rust 95aada11c4 (#38205 Enforce non-interactive approval policy for Codex delegates): Go subagent (delegate) sessions previously inherited the parent's approval policy, so approval-requiring commands and MCP tool calls could be forwarded to the parent. Implemented the central enforcement in prepareTurnStartParams: any subagent thread (subAgentThreadSpawn / Originator=subagent / subagent review-compact-other / memory consolidation sources) is pinned to approval_policy=never, mirroring Rust run_codex_thread_interactive (reject non-never + Constrained::allow_only(Never)). With never, Go already denies approval-requiring actions within the delegate (shell escalation reject, MCP elicitation auto-decline, network no-prompt, skill-MCP dependency skip) - now reachable for every delegate turn. Registered as contract delegate-noninteractive-approval-policy.

Ran the djalign method-4 CLI black-box differential as a live gate: Go code.exe vs the Rust @openai/codex release (v0.147.0) run through production ConPTY with /status + /mcp, comparing the observable TUI surface. The run surfaced two real issues, both fixed: (1) the differential test waited for the single identity marker 'gcode' on both binaries and asserted it on both - the Rust release brands itself 'OpenAI Codex' (documented allowed identity mapping rust codex <-> go gcode), so the test now waits for and asserts each side's own identity marker while keeping the shared /status+/mcp surface markers on both; (2) a real Go divergence: the Windows sandbox startup NUX opened even when the cwd was already trusted, while Rust gates it on onboarding_result.directory_trust_persisted (only a fresh/untrusted cwd produces a session trust decision, and elevated-required bypasses the gate). Go now mirrors the Rust condition ((trustDecision && level==Disabled) || elevatedRequired) via config.ProjectConfigEnabled (exported trust check) with the cwd resolved from root.Shared.CWD or os.Getwd(). Contracts cli-blackbox-slash-differential + windows-sandbox-nux-trust-decision; the gate is opt-in (CODEX_GO_SLASH_PARITY=1, both exes present) and token-free.

Aligned upstream 2bc43d516e (#38907 Edit queued messages with Vim history-up): Go's tea TUI lacked the edit_queued_message feature entirely. Implemented in the tea Model (applyEditQueuedMessageKey, routed before input-history navigation): the chat edit_queued_message binding (default alt-up / shift-left) restores the latest queued follow-up into the composer and removes it from the queue, and in Vim normal mode an empty composer's history-up binding (vim_normal move_up, default k/up) triggers the same restore - mirroring Rust chatwidget/interaction.rs. The restored message is removed from the queue so submitting the edited version replaces it instead of duplicating; remapped bindings are honored through the resolved keymap; the empty-composer gate preserves composer behavior when text is present. Registered as contract tui-edit-queued-message-vim-history-up with tests mirroring Rust composer_submission.rs (alt-up most-recent restore, edit-and-requeue cycle, remapped F2 binding, non-empty-composer guard).

items.reason: Closed the largest remaining internal TUI gap: Go's /vim was a stub (the vim_normal/vim_operator/vim_text_object actions were registered but never dispatched - only a flag toggled). Implemented a real Vim normal mode in the tea Model (tui/tea/vim_mode.go): a normal/insert mode state machine (Rust starts the composer in normal mode when /vim is enabled), dispatching the registered vim_normal actions through the resolved keymap - insert-entering (i/a/A/I/o/O/s/C), motions (h/l/k/j/w/b/e/0/$), edits (x/D), line yank (Y) + paste (p), and the dd/yy line-operator repeats (full operator + motion/text-object engine remains a tracked follow-up). Insert mode types normally until Esc; the #38907 queued-message history-up gate now requires real normal mode (not insert). Verified with 5 token-free tests (mode switching, word/line motions, edits, yank/paste, dd/yy, insert typing); the long-tail slash test was updated to enter insert mode before typing after /vim (correct Vim semantics). Registered as contract tui-vim-normal-mode.
